title: Consequences of implementing a cardiac troponin assay with improved sensitivity at Swedish coronary care units: an analysis from the SWEDEHEART registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective register-based before-and-after study; 37 710 coronary care unit admissions.
appraisal.main_limitation: Before-and-after design without a concurrent control, so secular change cannot be separated from the assay effect.
appraisal.one_line: SWEDEHEART analysis of the clinical consequences of moving to a more sensitive troponin assay in coronary care units.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: cTn levels above this cut-off exhibited stronger associations with mortality risk in study period 2 (adjusted HR 4.45 [95% CI 3.36-5.89]) compared with period 1 (adjusted HR 2.43 [95% CI 2.11-2.80]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Describes how sensitive assays shift identification of non-ACS troponin elevation and downstream invasive use.

title: Incident Type 2 Myocardial Infarction in a Cohort of Patients Undergoing Coronary or Peripheral Arterial Angiography.

appraisal.design_and_n: Single-centre prospective cohort; patients followed for a median of 3.4 years, of whom 152 (12.2%) had T2MI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre cohort of angiography patients, which limits generalisability to general type 2 MI.
appraisal.one_line: Cohort study of incident type 2 MI in patients undergoing angiography, with predictors and prognosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Incident diagnosis of T2MI strongly predicted risk for subsequent MACE (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.90; 95% confidence interval, 1.46-2.48; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies the poor prognosis of type 2 MI, a group without trial-based management.

title: Association of Postoperative High-Sensitivity Troponin Levels With Myocardial Injury and 30-Day Mortality Among Patients Undergoing Noncardiac Surgery.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective cohort at 23 centres in 13 countries, 21 842 participants aged 45 years or older.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational association; thresholds were derived in the same cohort.
appraisal.one_line: Postoperative hsTnT thresholds were associated with 30-day mortality in a large international cohort of noncardiac surgery patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Death within 30 days occurred in 266 patients (1.2%; 95% CI, 1.1%-1.4%); an absolute hsTnT change of 5 ng/L or higher was associated with an increased risk of 30-day mortality (adjusted HR, 4.69; 95% CI, 3.52-6.25).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Defines troponin thresholds for myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery, which underpin diagnosis and management decisions.

title: High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin and the Risk Stratification of Patients With Renal Impairment Presenting With Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre study of consecutive patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome, 4726 patients of whom 904 (19%) had renal impairment.
appraisal.main_limitation: Diagnostic accuracy study that does not test an outcome-driven pathway in renal impairment.
appraisal.one_line: High-sensitivity troponin I below 5 ng/L identified fewer low-risk patients with renal impairment but retained a high negative predictive value.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Troponin concentrations <5 ng/L at presentation identified 17% of patients with renal impairment as low risk for the primary outcome (negative predictive value, 98.4%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 96.0%-99.7%; sensitivity 98.9%; 95%CI, 97.5%-99.9%), in comparison with 56% without renal impairment.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs troponin pathways that determine invasive management in patients with CKD.

title: Discrimination of patients with type 2 myocardial infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective cohort of 1548 patients with suspected MI, of whom 99 had a final diagnosis of type 2 MI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest discrimination, a small number of type 2 MI cases and no external validation.
appraisal.one_line: Prospective emergency department cohort showed type 2 MI carried a 1-year mortality similar to type 1 MI and proposed a simple discrimination score.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients with T2MI showed a high 1-year mortality rate (13.8%), which equals that of T1MI patients (9.4%); the three-predictor score had an area under the curve of 0.71 to discriminate T1MI and T2MI.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Type 2 MI is common, poorly characterised and without trial-based management.

title: Perioperative Myocardial Injury After Noncardiac Surgery: Incidence, Mortality, and Characterization.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective diagnostic study, 2018 consecutive patients undergoing 2546 noncardiac surgeries.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-programme cohort in which management of injury was not randomised.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic troponin screening found perioperative myocardial injury in one in six surgeries, mostly without ischaemic symptoms, with high short- and long-term mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: PMI occurred after 397 of 2546 surgeries (16%; 95% confidence interval, 14%-17%); crude 30-day mortality was 8.9% (95% CI, 5.7-12.0) in patients with PMI versus 1.5% (95% CI, 0.9-2.0) in patients without PMI; adjusted hazard ratio of 2.7 (95% CI, 1.5-4.8).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Establishes the burden and prognosis of myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery, for which treatment evidence is lacking.

title: High-Sensitivity Troponins and Outcomes After Myocardial Infarction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Cohort study of all patients with a first MI in the Swedish National Patient Registry, 2009 to 2013; 47,133 MIs diagnosed using cTn and 40,746 using hs-cTnT.
appraisal.main_limitation: Before-and-after design vulnerable to temporal confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Swedish nationwide cohort assessing outcomes after introduction of high-sensitivity troponin T for MI diagnosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The rate of MI increased by 5% (95% CI: 0% to 10%) after the introduction of hs-cTnT. There was no difference in the risk of all-cause mortality (adjusted HR: 1.00; 95% CI: 0.97 to 1.02). The risk of reinfarction was reduced by 11% in patients diagnosed using hs-cTnT (adjusted HR: 0.89; 95% CI: 0.86 to 0.91).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows how troponin assay change was associated with more MI diagnoses and more invasive procedures.

title: Dabigatran in patients with myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery (MANAGE): an international, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: International, randomised, placebo-controlled trial at 84 hospitals in 19 countries; 1754 patients randomly assigned.
appraisal.main_limitation: High treatment discontinuation and a composite endpoint with modest event numbers.
appraisal.one_line: Placebo-controlled trial of dabigatran in patients with myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The composite primary efficacy outcome occurred in fewer patients randomised to dabigatran than placebo (97 [11%] of 877 patients assigned to dabigatran vs 133 [15%] of 877 patients assigned to placebo; hazard ratio [HR] 0·72, 95% CI 0·55-0·93; p=0·0115).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First randomised evidence for treating MINS, a common and under-addressed form of myocardial injury.

title: High-sensitivity troponin in the evaluation of patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome: a stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised controlled trial across ten hospitals in Scotland; 48 282 consecutive patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Outcome effect confined to reclassified patients and the assay changed diagnosis rather than a specific treatment.
appraisal.one_line: Stepped-wedge trial of implementing a high-sensitivity troponin assay in suspected ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In those reclassified, subsequent myocardial infarction or cardiovascular death within 1 year occurred in 105 (15%) of 720 patients in the validation phase and 131 (12%) of 1051 patients in the implementation phase (adjusted odds ratio for implementation vs validation phase 1·10, 95% CI 0·75 to 1·61; p=0·620).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to the downstream invasive management of patients with low-level troponin elevation.

title: Contemporary Diagnosis and Management of Patients With Myocardial Infarction in the Absence of Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; no sample size. States that MINOCA is found in ≈5% to 6% of all patients with acute infarction referred for coronary angiography.
appraisal.main_limitation: Statement relies on observational data and expert opinion, with little randomised evidence on management.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement provides an updated definition and diagnostic and management framework for MINOCA.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides a reference framework for a condition with scarce trial evidence and variable management.

title: Application of High-Sensitivity Troponin in Suspected Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Derivation-validation design in 22,651 patients (9604 in the derivation data set and 13,047 in the validation data set).
appraisal.main_limitation: Diagnostic accuracy study without a randomised test of the pathway.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled analysis of 15 cohorts deriving and validating a high-sensitivity troponin risk tool for suspected myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: High-sensitivity troponin I concentrations of less than 6 ng per liter and an absolute change of less than 4 ng per liter after 45 to 120 minutes resulted in a negative predictive value of 99.5% for myocardial infarction, with an associated 30-day risk of subsequent myocardial infarction or death of 0.2%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports early rule-out in the emergency department and downstream invasive decisions.

title: High-Sensitivity Troponin and the Application of Risk Stratification Thresholds in Patients With Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre trial cohort across 10 hospitals in Scotland, 32 837 consecutive patients included (n=48 282 enrolled).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational secondary analysis of a single assay (Abbott hs-cTnI) in a single country.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified observational secondary analysis of a large trial cohort comparing hs-cTnI thresholds of <5 ng/L and <2 ng/L for rule-out in suspected ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The negative predictive value for the primary outcome was 99.8% (95% CI, 99.7%-99.8%) and 99.9% (95% CI, 99.8%-99.9%) in those with hs-cTnl concentrations of <5 ng/L and <2 ng/L, respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a higher rule-out threshold that would allow more patients to be discharged safely from the ACS pathway.

title: A Randomized Trial of a 1-Hour Troponin T Protocol in Suspected Acute Coronary Syndromes: The Rapid Assessment of Possible Acute Coronary Syndrome in the Emergency Department With High-Sensitivity Troponin T Study (RAPID-TnT).

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre patient-level randomised noninferiority trial, 3378 randomly assigned (n=1646 vs n=1642 analysed).
appraisal.main_limitation: Low event rate for the 30-day death or MI endpoint and a standard arm that masked troponin values below 30 ng/L.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of a 0/1-hour hs-cTnT protocol in suspected ACS found it non-inferior to 0/3-hour masked testing at 30 days, with faster discharge.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 0/1-hour hs-cTnT protocol was not inferior to standard care (0/1-hour arm: 17/1646 [1.0%] versus 16/1642 [1.0%]; incidence rate ratio, 1.06 [ 0.53-2.11], noninferiority P value=0.006, superiority P value=0.867), although an increase in myocardial injury was observed.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows that rapid troponin pathways shorten ED stay, while newly recognised troponin elevation raises management questions relevant to myocardial injury.

title: High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin and the Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified secondary analysis of a stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial, 48 282 consecutive patients with suspected ACS.
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary analysis comparing diagnostic categories rather than a randomised comparison of treatments.
appraisal.one_line: High-STEACS secondary analysis found that implementing hs-cTn and the Universal Definition increased diagnoses of type 2 MI and myocardial injury without changes in investigation, treatment or outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Implementation increased the diagnosis of type 1 myocardial infarction by 11% (510/4471), type 2 myocardial infarction by 22% (205/916), and acute and chronic myocardial injury by 36% (443/1233) and 43% (389/898), respectively. Despite modest increases in antiplatelet therapy and coronary revascularization after implementation in patients with type 1 myocardial infarction, the primary outcome was unchanged (cause specific HR 1.00 [95% CI, 0.82-1.21]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Documents the unmet treatment need in type 2 MI and myocardial injury and motivates trials of management in those groups.

title: Sex-Specific Thresholds of High-Sensitivity Troponin in Patients With Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial across 10 hospitals; 48,282 patients (47% women).
appraisal.main_limitation: Sex-specific analysis of a diagnostic implementation trial, not a treatment trial.
appraisal.one_line: High-STEACS analysis of sex-specific hs-cTnI thresholds found more women identified with myocardial injury but unchanged outcomes and less treatment than men.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Use of the high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I assay with sex-specific thresholds increased myocardial injury in women by 42% and in men by 6%. The primary outcome occurred in 18% (369 of 2,072) and 17% (488 of 2,919) of women with myocardial injury before and after implementation, respectively (adjusted hazard ratio: 1.11; 95% confidence interval: 0.92 to 1.33).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows an under-treatment gap in women with myocardial injury that is a target for sex-specific research.

title: Initial Imaging-Guided Strategy Versus Routine Care in Patients With Non-ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised controlled trial, 207 patients with elevated hs-cTnT and inconclusive ECG.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre-scale sample of 207 patients, too small for clinical outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Small RCT found CMR-first or CTA-first strategies cut invasive angiography in NSTEMI without a difference in 1-year outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The CMR- and CTA-first strategies reduced ICA compared with routine clinical care (87% [p = 0.001], 66% [p < 0.001], and 100%, respectively), with similar outcome (hazard ratio: CMR vs. routine, 0.78 [95% confidence interval: 0.37 to 1.61]; CTA vs. routine, 0.66 [95% confidence interval: 0.31 to 1.42]; and CMR vs. CTA, 1.19 [95% confidence interval: 0.53 to 2.66]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges routine invasive angiography in troponin-positive chest pain, relevant to selection for an invasive strategy.

title: The effect of remote ischaemic preconditioning on myocardial injury in emergency hip fracture surgery (PIXIE trial): phase II randomised clinical trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Phase II multicentre randomised, observer-blinded trial; 648 randomised, 573 in the intention-to-treat analysis (286 RIPC, 287 control).
appraisal.main_limitation: The primary outcome definition was changed during the trial and clinical outcomes were underpowered.
appraisal.one_line: PIXIE phase II trial found remote ischaemic preconditioning reduced myocardial injury after emergency hip fracture surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 25 of 168 (15%) patients in the RIPC group and 45 of 158 (28%) in the control group (odds ratio 0.44, 95% confidence interval 0.25 to 0.76; P=0.003). The revised primary outcome occurred in 57 of 286 patients (20%) in the RIPC group and 90 of 287 (31%) in the control group (0.55, 0.37 to 0.80; P=0.002).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to perioperative myocardial injury, though CONDI-2 was neutral for clinical outcomes in STEMI.

title: Incidence, Trends, and Outcomes of Type 2 Myocardial Infarction in a Community Cohort.

appraisal.design_and_n: Olmsted County, Minnesota community cohort; 5460 patients with at least one cardiac troponin T ≥0.01 ng/mL, of whom 1365 were classified as index T1MI and 1054 as T2MI (2003 to 2012).
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-community cohort with retrospective adjudication of type, so misclassification is possible.
appraisal.one_line: Population-based cohort estimating incidence, trends and long-term outcomes of type 2 myocardial infarction compared with type 1.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The annual incidence of T1MI decreased markedly from 202 to 84 per 100 000 persons between 2003 and 2012 (P<0.001), whereas the incidence of T2MI declined from 130 to 78 per 100 000 persons (P=0.02). Rates of cardiovascular death were similar after either type of MI (hazard ratio, 0.8 [95% CI, 0.7-1.0], P=0.11).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives population-level incidence and prognosis for a common condition with no established treatment, informing trial design.

title: Cardiovascular Mortality After Type 1 and Type 2 Myocardial Infarction in Young Adults.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Cohort of 3,829 adults aged 50 years or younger, adjudicated using the Fourth Universal Definition; median follow-up 10.2 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with non-cardiac comorbidity driving much of the excess mortality.
appraisal.one_line: Adjudicated cohort showing higher long-term mortality after type 2 MI and myocardial injury than type 1 MI in young adults.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Type 2 MI was associated with higher all-cause (hazard ratio: 1.8; 95% confidence interval: 1.2 to 2.7; p = 0.004) and cardiovascular mortality (hazard ratio: 2.7; 95% confidence interval: 1.4 to 5.1; p = 0.003) compared with type 1 MI.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Highlights a high-risk group in whom no evidence-based management exists and who received fewer cardiovascular medications.

title: High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin on Presentation to Rule Out Myocardial Infarction: A Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Stepped-wedge cluster randomised trial in 7 Scottish hospitals; 31 492 patients; NCT03005158.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-inferiority not shown at 30 days; pathway effect is health-system specific.
appraisal.one_line: Stepped-wedge cluster trial: early hs-troponin rule-out pathway shortened stay and raised discharge but did not show 30-day non-inferiority for safety.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Length of stay was reduced from 10.1±4.1 to 6.8±3.9 hours (adjusted geometric mean ratio, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.73-0.83]). Noninferiority was not demonstrated for the 30-day safety outcome (upper limit of 1-sided 95% CI for adjusted risk difference, 0.70% [noninferiority margin 0.50%]; P=0.068).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Troponin pathway design affects who proceeds to invasive assessment.

title: Late Outcomes of the RAPID-TnT Randomized Controlled Trial: 0/1-Hour High-Sensitivity Troponin T Protocol in Suspected ACS.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised multicentre trial; 3378 randomised, 3270 with 12-month follow-up; ACTRN12615001379505.
appraisal.main_limitation: Late outcomes are secondary analyses; subgroup finding unadjusted.
appraisal.one_line: RAPID-TnT: 0/1-hour hs-cTnT protocol did not reduce ischaemic events at 12 months and was linked to more death or MI in those with troponin in the masked range.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows troponin reporting protocols can change invasive testing and later events.

title: Prognostically relevant periprocedural myocardial injury and infarction associated with percutaneous coronary interventions: a Consensus Document of the ESC Working Group on Cellular Biology of the Heart and European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI).

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Thresholds rely on expert consensus and limited data, as the document states.
appraisal.one_line: ESC/EAPCI consensus document on prognostically relevant periprocedural myocardial injury and infarction after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Proposes a troponin threshold of more than 5 times the 99th percentile for major periprocedural injury.

title: Cardiac Troponin Thresholds and Kinetics to Differentiate Myocardial Injury and Myocardial Infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a multicentre randomised trial (NCT01852123); 46 092 consecutive patients, 8188 with troponin above the 99th percentile.
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary analysis; diagnostic adjudication drives the reference standard.
appraisal.one_line: In 46 092 patients, admission troponin alone did not separate type 1 MI from type 2 MI or myocardial injury; kinetics added modest discrimination.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 99th percentile and rule-in thresholds gave positive predictive values of 57% (95% CI, 56%-58%), 59% (58%-61%) and 62% (60%-64%). Combining concentration and change gave AUC 0.661 [0.642-0.680] versus 0.613 [0.594-0.633].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Troponin thresholds should not drive invasive management in isolation in type 2 MI and injury.

title: Risk factors for type 1 and type 2 myocardial infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a multicentre randomised trial population, 48 282 patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome; 924 type 1 and 407 type 2 myocardial infarctions within 1 year.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational analysis within a trial cohort, so the associations are not causal and residual confounding is possible.
appraisal.one_line: Secondary analysis of a large randomised cohort found that risk factors for type 1 and type 2 myocardial infarction were largely similar.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The strongest predictor of type 2 myocardial infarction was a prior history of type 2 events (aHR 6.18, 95% CI 4.70-8.12); sex was not a predictor of type 2 events (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.66-1.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large adjudicated cohort for type 2 myocardial infarction, a poorly evidenced area where treatment of shared risk factors might be tested.

title: Diagnosis and Management of Patients With Myocardial Injury After Noncardiac Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus statement, so recommendations rest on limited trial evidence.
appraisal.one_line: American Heart Association scientific statement on diagnosis, surveillance and treatment of myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract states that myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery occurs in ≈20% of patients who have major inpatient surgery; it does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets out diagnostic criteria and management for a common, prognostically important condition lacking trial-based treatment.

title: High-Sensitivity Troponin I after Cardiac Surgery and 30-Day Mortality.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: International prospective cohort study (VISION Cardiac Surgery) of 13,862 patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational association with mortality; thresholds have wide confidence intervals and the study does not test an intervention.
appraisal.one_line: International prospective cohort relating peak high-sensitivity troponin I after cardiac surgery to 30-day mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among patients who underwent isolated coronary-artery bypass grafting or aortic-valve replacement or repair, the threshold troponin level, measured within 1 day after surgery, that was associated with an adjusted hazard ratio of more than 1.00 for death within 30 days was 5670 ng per liter (95% confidence interval [CI], 1045 to 8260), a level 218 times the upper reference limit. Among patients who underwent other cardiac surgery, the corresponding threshold was 12,981 ng per liter (95% CI, 2673 to 16,591), a level 499 times the upper reference limit.
appraisal.why_it_matters: The mortality-associated thresholds are far above those used to define periprocedural myocardial injury, which bears on definitions and on triggers for invasive investigation after surgical revascularisation.

title: Coronary Artery and Cardiac Disease in Patients With Type 2 Myocardial Infarction: A Prospective Cohort Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective cohort study; 8064 consecutive patients with raised troponin screened, 100 with a provisional diagnosis of type 2 myocardial infarction.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample with exclusion of frail patients and those with renal or hepatic failure.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic coronary and cardiac imaging in patients with type 2 myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The prevalence of coronary artery disease was 68% (63 of 93), which was obstructive in 30% (28 of 93). Coronary artery disease and left ventricular systolic dysfunction were previously unrecognized in 60% (38 of 63) and 84% (27 of 32), respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It indicates substantial unrecognised coronary and myocardial disease in type 2 MI, informing whether invasive assessment is warranted.

title: Long-term outcomes of perioperative myocardial infarction/injury after non-cardiac surgery.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre cohort of 7754 high-risk patients undergoing major non-cardiac surgery; perioperative MI/injury occurred in 1016 (13.1%).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design; aetiology adjudication depended on clinically indicated work-up.
appraisal.one_line: Aetiology-specific one-year outcomes of perioperative myocardial infarction and injury after non-cardiac surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At least one MACE occurred in 684/7754 patients (8.8%) and 818/7754 patients died (10.5%) within 1 year; MACE occurred in 51%, 41%, 57%, 64%, and 25% of extra-cardiac PMI, T1MI, tachyarrhythmia, AHF, and lT2MI respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Outcomes differ sharply by aetiology, which is relevant to selecting patients for investigation and treatment.

title: Machine learning for diagnosis of myocardial infarction using cardiac troponin concentrations.

appraisal.design_and_n: Models trained on 10,038 patients and externally validated in 10,286 patients from seven cohorts.
appraisal.main_limitation: Diagnostic modelling study; the abstract does not describe a prospective trial of its effect on clinical decisions or outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Machine learning score (CoDE-ACS) integrating troponin with clinical features to diagnose myocardial infarction, externally validated.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: CoDE-ACS had area under curve 0.953 (95% confidence interval, 0.947-0.958) for myocardial infarction and classified 61 versus 27% of patients at presentation as low probability compared with fixed troponin thresholds, with similar negative predictive value.
appraisal.why_it_matters: A validated probability approach could change rule-out and rule-in pathways and so the volume of patients referred for invasive assessment.

title: Troponin in early presenters to rule out myocardial infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Diagnostic cohort of 41 103 consecutive patients, 12 595 presenting within 3 h, 3728 with myocardial infarction, with external validation in 7088 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Diagnostic accuracy study of one assay; outcomes after rule-out were not the primary focus in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: Evaluation of single high-sensitivity troponin I thresholds for rule-out of MI in patients presenting early after symptom onset.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In those presenting ≤3 h, a threshold of 2 ng/L had sensitivity 99.4% (95% confidence interval 99.2%-99.5%) and negative predictive value 99.7% (99.6%-99.8%) compared with 5 ng/L [96.5% (96.2%-96.8%) and 99.3% (99.1%-99.4%)].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Clarifies which troponin thresholds permit safe single-sample rule-out in early presenters.

title: Accelerated -Rule-Out of acute Myocardial Infarction using prehospital copeptin and in-hospital troponin: The AROMI study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial in 4351 patients with suspected AMI transported by ambulance.
appraisal.main_limitation: Shorter stay is a process endpoint, and the noninferiority margin is not given in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of accelerated rule-out of MI using prehospital copeptin plus hs-troponin T.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The accelerated strategy reduced mean length of stay by 0.9 h (95% confidence interval 0.7-1.1 h) and was non-inferior regarding 30-day major adverse cardiac events (absolute risk difference -0.4%, 95% confidence interval -2.5 to 1.7; P-value for non-inferiority = 0.013).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to troponin-based pathways that determine who proceeds to invasive assessment.

title: High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin for Risk Assessment in Patients With Chronic Coronary Artery Disease.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective cohort of 4,240 patients attending outpatient coronary angiography, 3,888 with coronary artery disease and 255 (6%) primary outcome events, median follow-up 2.4 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Prognostic association only; the abstract states that whether testing could inform treatment intensification remains untested.
appraisal.one_line: Blinded prospective cohort testing high-sensitivity troponin I for risk stratification in chronic coronary artery disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Troponin concentrations were associated with the primary outcome after adjusting for cardiovascular risk factors and coronary artery disease severity (adjusted HR: 2.3; 95% CI: 1.7-3.0, log10 troponin; P < 0.001). A troponin concentration >10 ng/L identified patients with a 50% increase in the risk of myocardial infarction or cardiovascular death.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a trial of troponin-guided treatment intensification in chronic coronary disease.

title: Effect of colchicine on perioperative atrial fibrillation and myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery in patients undergoing major thoracic surgery (COP-AF): an international randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: International randomised trial of 3209 patients undergoing major thoracic surgery.
appraisal.main_limitation: Neither primary endpoint was significantly reduced.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of colchicine for perioperative atrial fibrillation and myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MINS occurred in 295 (18·3%) patients assigned to colchicine and 325 (20·3%) patients assigned to placebo (HR 0·89, 0·76 to 1·05; ARR 2·0%, -0·8 to 4·7; p=0·16).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Reports on a pharmacological approach to myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery.

title: Coronary Computed Tomographic Angiography With Fractional Flow Reserve in Patients With Type 2 Myocardial Infarction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective single-study enrolment of 50 participants meeting Fourth Universal Definition criteria for type 2 MI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample without outcome data; no evidence on whether revascularisation or other therapy changes outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Prospective coronary CTA with FFRCT in adjudicated type 2 MI to describe the prevalence and haemodynamic significance of CAD.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Coronary CTA revealed coronary plaque in 46 participants (92%). A moderate or greater stenosis (≥50%) was identified in 42% of participants, and obstructive disease was present in 26%. A hemodynamically significant focal stenosis identified by FFRCT was present in 13 participants (26%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Describes coronary substrate in type 2 MI, a population lacking trials to inform invasive evaluation.

title: Implementation of a high sensitivity cardiac troponin I assay and risk of myocardial infarction or death at five years: observational analysis of a stepped wedge, cluster randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational analysis of a stepped wedge trial; 10 360 patients had cardiac troponin concentrations greater than the 99th centile, of whom 1771 (17.1%) were reclassified.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational comparison of before and after periods with potential temporal confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Observational analysis of a stepped wedge cluster randomised trial of high-sensitivity troponin I implementation and five-year outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Five year incidence of subsequent myocardial infarction or death was 29.4% (5588/18 978) v 25.9% (7591/29 304) in all patients (adjusted hazard ratio 0.97, 95% confidence interval 0.93 to 1.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs outcomes of reclassified patients with myocardial injury and type 2 MI.

title: Periprocedural myocardial infarction after percutaneous coronary intervention and long-term mortality: a meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: 19 studies and 109 568 patients included.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational pooled data using adjusted estimates with considerable heterogeneity for the SCAI definition.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of 19 studies reports that periprocedural MI under three definitions was associated with higher all-cause mortality after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All PMI definitions were independently associated with all-cause mortality [UDMI: hazard ratio (HR) 1.61, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.32-1.97; I2 34%; ARC-2: HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.40-3.08, I2 0%; SCAI: HR 3.24, 95% CI 2.36-4.44, I2 78%].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs which periprocedural MI definition should anchor trial endpoints and clinical decisions.

title: Restrictive Versus Liberal Transfusion in Patients With Type 1 or Type 2 Myocardial Infarction: A Prespecified Analysis of the MINT Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Type 1 (n=1460) and type 2 (n=1955) MI with anaemia randomly allocated to restrictive or liberal transfusion.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis with a non-significant interaction test, so the type-specific effects are hypothesis-generating.
appraisal.one_line: A prespecified MINT analysis suggests the harm signal with restrictive transfusion in MI with anaemia was more apparent in type 1 than type 2 MI, without a significant interaction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The rate of death or MI was higher in patients with type 1 MI randomized to a restrictive (18.2%) versus liberal (13.8%) transfusion strategy (relative risk [RR], 1.32 [95% CI, 1.04-1.67]) with no difference observed between the restrictive (15.8%) and liberal (15.1%) transfusion strategies in patients with type 2 MI (RR, 1.05 [95% CI, 0.85-1.29]). The test for a differential effect of transfusion strategy by MI type was not statistically significant (Pinteraction = 0.16).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives rare randomised evidence on type 2 MI management.

title: Prognostic Relevance of Type 4a Myocardial Infarction and Periprocedural Myocardial Injury in Patients With Non-ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consecutive cohort of 1412 patients with NSTEMI undergoing PCI; internal validation cohort of 305 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre observational data with internal validation only.
appraisal.one_line: Single-centre cohort proposing a post-PCI troponin I threshold for prognostically relevant periprocedural injury in NSTEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A post-PCI ΔcTnI >20% but ≤40% showed similar outcomes to patients without PMI, whereas >40% was identified as the optimal threshold for prognostically relevant PMI. The abstract does not report an effect estimate with a confidence interval.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the definition of type 4a MI and periprocedural injury in patients with elevated baseline troponin, where the Universal Definition is ambiguous.

title: Effect of Remote Ischemic Preconditioning on Myocardial Injury in Noncardiac Surgery: The PRINCE Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multinational double-blind randomized trial; 1213 patients (599 RIPC, 614 sham).
appraisal.main_limitation: Myocardial injury endpoint rather than clinical events.
appraisal.one_line: PRINCE found remote ischaemic preconditioning did not reduce myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Postoperative myocardial injury occurred in 215 of 566 patients (38.0%) in the RIPC group and in 223 of 596 patients (37.4%) in the sham RIPC group (relative risk, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.88-1.18; P=0.84).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large neutral trial relevant to perioperative myocardial injury prevention.

title: Ivabradine in Patients Undergoing Noncardiac Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre double-blind placebo-controlled RCT, 2101 participants randomised.
appraisal.main_limitation: Stopped at interim analysis for futility, and the primary outcome is myocardial injury rather than a clinical event.
appraisal.one_line: Perioperative ivabradine did not reduce myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery and the trial stopped for futility.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MINS occurred in 178 of 1050 patients (17.0%) in the ivabradine group and in 159 of 1051 patients (15.1%) in the placebo group (relative risk, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.92 to 1.37]; P=0.25).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Closes off heart rate lowering with ivabradine as a strategy to prevent perioperative myocardial injury.

title: Cardiovascular Risk Across Myocardial Injury and Infarction Categories Using the Universal Definition: An Individual Patient-Level Data Meta-Analysis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review with IPD meta-analysis, 17 studies of 9 cohorts, 120,734 patients with IPD in 8 cohorts.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational cohorts with high heterogeneity for type 1 MI, and results show association rather than treatment effect.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of patient-level data from cohorts found high MACE rates across type 1 MI, type 2 MI, and acute and chronic myocardial injury.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with those without myocardial injury, the risk of MACE (subdistribution HR) was 4.82 (95% CI: 3.55-6.57; I2 = 84%) in type 1 MI and 3.36 (95% CI: 2.92-3.86; I2 = 0%) in type 2 MI.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies prognosis of type 2 MI and myocardial injury, supporting trials of management strategies in these groups.

title: Comparison of the European Society of Cardiology 0/1-Hour and High-Sensitivity Troponin in the Evaluation of Patients With Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome 0/2-or-0/3-Hour Algorithms for Rapid Myocardial Infarction Diagnosis: A Prospective Multicenter Study.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective international multicentre diagnostic study of 4,663 eligible patients, 663 (14.2%) with NSTEMI type 1, with external validation (n = 2,485).
appraisal.main_limitation: Diagnostic accuracy study without randomised comparison of clinical outcomes under each pathway.
appraisal.one_line: Head-to-head diagnostic comparison of the ESC 0/1-hour algorithm and the High-STEACS 0/2-hour or 0/3-hour pathway in suspected NSTEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The ESC 0/1h-algorithm had higher sensitivity when using hs-cTnI-Architect (100% [95% CI: 99.4-100]) compared with the High-STEACS 0/2h-pathway (98.1% [95% CI: 96.7-99], P < 0.001), but the proportion of patients assigned to the rule-out group was lower (52% vs 72.5%, P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses guideline discordance on rapid NSTEMI rule-out that determines who proceeds to invasive assessment.

title: The Burden of Type 1 Peri-Operative Myocardial Infarction After Non-Cardiac Surgery: Insights From the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project From 2010-2023.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort (Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project linked to Hospital Episode Statistics); 2,821 episodes of type 1 PMI in 533,026 eligible patients (0.5%).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry data restricted to type 1 PMI recorded in the audit, with residual confounding and likely under-ascertainment of perioperative events.
appraisal.one_line: Registry-linked cohort of type 1 perioperative MI after non-cardiac surgery in England, reporting short- and long-term mortality by operation type.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Risk of thirty-day mortality was significantly higher in PMI patients at thirty-days (adjusted Hazard Ratio):1.34 [95% CIs 1.21-1.49]) and five-years (1.36 [1.29-1.43]) (both P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies the long-term mortality associated with type 1 perioperative MI and its variation by surgical specialty, relevant to invasive management pathways after noncardiac surgery.

title: ICare-FASTER (Improving Care by Faster Risk Stratification Through Use of High-Sensitivity Point-of-Care Troponin in Patients Presenting With Possible Acute Coronary Syndrome in the Emergency Department): A Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomized Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pragmatic stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial, six sites, 59 980 ED presentations (44 747 individuals).
appraisal.main_limitation: The primary outcome is a process measure (length of stay) and the safety outcome has very few events.
appraisal.one_line: Stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial of point-of-care hs-cTnI in an accelerated ED pathway shortened ED length of stay without a difference in 30-day MI or cardiac death.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The intervention reduced length of stay by 13% (95% CI, 9%-16%; P<0.001), corresponding to a reduction of 47 minutes (95% CI, 33-61 minutes) from a mean length of stay in the control arm of 376 minutes. The 30-day myocardial infarction or cardiac death rate was similar in the control and intervention arms (0.39% and 0.39%, respectively; P=0.54).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports point-of-care troponin pathways in emergency departments, which determine the front end of invasive management for suspected MI.
